_doc: Amane's openers (Amane.opener -> TownTalk.line_in): {when, t, cool, once}. The rule with the most matching criteria wins, said lines rest `cool` days (default 5). Criteria: everything TownTalk knows (period, place, rain, route, flag, week_min...) plus tears_min/max, bond_min/max, self_min, jealousy_min, cat_nights_min, promise_steps. The old data/amane.json openers stay as the fallback. One rule per line.

t: Senpai! I made too much rice this morning. It's not for you. ...It's for you.
Hi, Senpai. I wasn't waiting. I just happened to be here. For forty minutes.
Senpai, your tie is crooked. Can I-- no. Sorry. Never mind.
I found a four-leaf clover. I'm keeping it in my notebook. Next to your timetable. I mean-- next to MY timetable.
Senpai. Hello. I practised saying hello. That one was the good version.
Oh! Senpai. What a coincidence. I've been coincidentally here since lunch.
G-good morning, Senpai. The cats said you'd come this way. I mean - I guessed.
Morning, Senpai. Your hair's sticking up at the back. It's nice. Leave it.
Senpai, there's a seat by the window on the roof where the wind doesn't reach. I've been keeping it warm.
Did you eat? You didn't eat. I can tell. I brought two onigiri. Just in case. In case of you.
School's over. The best part of the day starts now. ...Is that weird to say?
Senpai! Are you going home? Which way? No reason. I'm going that way too. Every way, actually.
It's the red hour, Senpai. Omagatoki. Things can see us now. Stay where I can see you.
Look - the lanterns on the steps are coming on. One by one. I used to count them, waiting.
It's late, Senpai. You should be home. ...I'll walk behind you. To make sure. Not following. Escorting.
The town's asleep. The cats aren't. Neither am I.
No school today! I didn't know what to do with my face all morning, so I came to find you.
It's a holiday. Grandma says I should 'do something normal'. Is this normal? Talking to you?
The shrine's quiet today. Grandma's feeding the cats. Every cat. There are so many cats.
Did you climb all the steps? Nine hundred and ninety-nine. Don't count past that, Senpai. Promise.
The river's high. When I was small I thought it went all the way to the other side. It does, sort of.
Gataro waved at me. The kappa. He only waves at people he likes. He likes you too, I think.
The station smells like rain and old tickets. I don't like it here. People leave from here.
Don't take the last train, Senpai. Not ever. ...Sorry. That came out strange.
The sea's loud today. Grandma says it's counting the boats.
If you stand where the waves end, the sand pulls at your feet. Like it wants you to stay. I understand the sand.
Everyone on the street knows your name now. They say it like you've always lived here.
The dango shop gave me a free one because I said I knew you. Is that allowed?
It's just the season, Senpai. Ignore the rain. Please. Ignore it really hard.
My hood's wet. It's not from crying. It's from the sky. The sky is also not crying.
I'm f-fine. It's raining because it's June. Or April. Whatever month it is, it's that.
Don't look at me right now. Look at the cats. The cats are nicer to look at.
It's sunny. Did you notice? I noticed. I've been noticing all day.
No rain today. Grandma hung the futons out. She looked at me like I did something.
Senpai. Can I say something embarrassing? ...Never mind. Saying 'can I say something' was the embarrassing part.
When you laughed yesterday I wrote down the time. That's not strange. That's research.
I like this. Just this. Standing here with you while nothing happens.
Senpai, if I asked you to stay a bit longer, would you? You don't have to answer. Just stay.
Senpai... are you angry with me? You can say. I'd rather know than guess. I'm bad at guessing. I guess all night.
I'll stand further away today. Is here good? Here?
Senpai! You're here! ...I mean. Hello. Normally.
I saved you a seat on the roof. And the seat next to it, so nobody else sits there.
Hold still - there's a petal on your shoulder. ...Got it. I'm keeping it.
Senpai, I sat with someone from my class at lunch. We didn't talk. But it counts, right?
Kuroe-senpai told me a ghost story and I wasn't scared. I was a little scared. I told her a better one.
Senpai. Did I do something today? Tell me what and I won't do it again.
I won't bother you. I'm just... going the same way. Every way.
Hayate-senpai said hello to me today. On purpose. I said hello back. Is that what friends do? It felt like what friends do.
You're my friend. I checked. I asked the cats.
You laughed with {rival_short}-senpai today. Thirty-one seconds. I wasn't counting. The cats were.
{rival_short}-senpai walks very close to you. Very close. I measured. With my eyes.
I wasn't jealous. I was just standing behind the vending machine for an hour. Being normal.
Is {rival_short}-senpai your best friend? You can have two. You can have... one and a half.
I heard about {rival_short}-senpai. I-it wasn't me. I was asleep. I'm always asleep when it happens.
Is {rival_short}-senpai okay? Everyone says it was an accident. I keep dreaming it wasn't.
Nobody can find {rival_short}-senpai. The cats won't look at me. Senpai, I don't know where my dreams go at night.
I had a dream I was a cat on a roof. I was so angry and I didn't know why. Then I woke up and my feet were dirty.
Senpai, do you ever dream you're somewhere else? I dream I'm on the roofs. Every night now.
You were so fast at practice! I watched from the fence. The fence is a public place.
Hayate-senpai makes you run so much. Do your legs hurt? I could carry your bag. I'm stronger than I look. I'm not.
The Go-Home Club president requests the treasurer's company on the way home. That's an official request.
I can hear the bamboo swords from outside the budokan. Every hit, I flinch. Please don't get hurt.
Are you writing about me in the paper? Don't. Or do. Use a nice photo.
You work at night now? Then I'll walk past the window at night. Only once. Only a few times.
You were late again! Makabe-sensei looked at the door like it had insulted him. Next time I'll wake you. I know where you live. Everyone does.
You weren't in class. I looked. I asked the cats. They said you were by the river doing nothing. Is that true?
Makabe-sensei said you answered a question right. He was so surprised he dropped the chalk.
Grandma says you've been asking about the old days. Be careful what you remember, Senpai. Remembering is how it starts.
The bell rang by itself last night. Grandma pretended not to hear. She hears everything.
Golden Week! The shopping street's full of stalls. Do you like candied apples? I've never had one with someone.
Exams soon. I made you flashcards. Every card says 'you can do it' on the back. Even the history ones.
It's rainy season. Everyone blames the season. I'm grateful to the season.
The sports festival's coming. If you run, I'll cheer. Quietly. Very loudly in my head.
{days_left} days until Tanabata. I've written my wish already. I wrote it very small so the gods have to lean in.
You promised to come to the steps on the seventh. I'm not reminding you. I'm just saying it out loud so it's real.
You didn't eat anything over there. On the other side. I could tell. You came back all of you.
You ate something on the other side, didn't you? You smell like festival sugar. Don't go back without me.
Rin talked to you? She doesn't talk to anyone. She used to talk to me, when I was a cat. She was rude then too.
You remember now. Don't you. The steps, the summer you were seven. You look at me differently.
My mother's home. My actual mother. She burns the rice. I've never been so happy about burnt rice.
Tonight's Tanabata. I'll be on the steps. I'll be there however long it takes. That's the one thing I'm good at.
